surface: Shared Source recognition in Scrape and chat page context
auth_mode: guest and authenticated member across multiple organizations
reproduction: With a valid session but no selected organization on this device, look up a URL that is saved in one of multiple RLS-visible organizations.

The prior lookup catches an organization-resolution error as null, conditionally omits organization_id from the docproc read, and may claim the other organization's Source as saved in the current workspace.
The Scrape recognition hook also watches only the tab URL, so a workspace switch on the same page can leave the prior workspace's saved claim visible.
The background saved-page broadcast carries no organization, so a late event from the prior workspace can overwrite a new workspace's recognition state.
Scrape's local Saved button and Source link can remain bound to A after switching to B, or be restored by an A Save that finishes late; an overlapping B retry must remain queued.
expected: Guest recognition returns none without a read. Authenticated recognition reads only the selected organization; missing or unreadable selection returns an honest unknown without a docproc read. Switching organization clears stale recognition, starts a scoped recheck, and ignores an older lookup or background broadcast that finishes late.
actual: The shared query can read without an organization predicate, and the hook can retain a prior organization's claim after selection changes.
severity: S2: wrong-workspace Saved claim may reveal another RLS-visible organization's Source identity and misstate capture status
priority: P1: close the organization boundary before claiming workspace-correct recognition
